- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending up.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias starting from day 10–15 of forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overreact to short-term sentiment; for 30d, apply 50% weight to recent 7-day sentiment trend vs 50% to 30d history.
